image_description: A bassoon standing vertically against a wall in a dimly lit room. The instrument features a dark reddish-brown wooden body with complex silver metal keywork. A curved metal bocal is attached to the top joint, and the bell points upward. The background includes a white textured wall on the left and dark shadows/cardboard boxes on the right.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Long wooden wind instrument of considerable height when assembled.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The instrument spans nearly the full height of the frame, consistent with the ~1.3m length of a bassoon.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Distinctive U-shape when viewed from front with bell pointing upward.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The boot joint at the bottom connects the long wing joint and butt joint, creating the characteristic U-fold structure. The bell is clearly visible at the top right.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Conical bore that doubles back on itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The internal bore structure is not visible from the exterior view; this feature cannot be visually verified without an X-ray or cutaway view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Curved metal bocal mouthpiece tube at top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A distinct curved metal tube (bocal) protrudes from the upper wing joint, ready for a reed.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Numerous metal keys and tone holes distributed along length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Complex silver keywork with rods and levers is densely distributed along the wooden body, matching the mechanical complexity of a real bassoon.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bell flares outward at top and instrument held diagonally across body when played.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bell flare is visible at the top. While not being played, the instrument's resting diagonal orientation against the wall is physically plausible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dark reddish-brown polished wood finish maple or rosewood.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The wood exhibits a deep reddish-brown hue with specular highlights indicating a polished varnish finish, consistent with maple or rosewood.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Metal keys are silver or gold-plated.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The keys reflect light with a cool, silvery tone, indicating nickel-silver or silver plating.
The main body segments are clearly constructed from turned wood.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The white wall has a slightly repetitive, noisy texture pattern that lacks natural plaster variation, suggesting minor generative noise or compression artifacts, though it does not affect the subject.
The dark area on the right lacks detail and fades into pure black somewhat unnaturally, possibly due to lighting simulation issues, but no structural melting is observed.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific taxonomic classification of the instrument and rule out look-alikes like contrabassoon or fake props.
To verify that the complex metal keys are physically connected to the wooden body and do not float or merge incorrectly.
To ensure the instrument sits correctly in 3D space against the wall and does not exhibit foreground-background bleeding.
To assess overall lighting consistency and detect any subtle global artifacts missed by specific auditors.

focus_areas: Connectivity of metal keys to wooden body
Physical plausibility of the bocal attachment
Consistency of wood grain and polish reflections
Separation of instrument from dark background
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'keywork' topology. AI often struggles with the intricate linkage of bassoon keys. Verify if any keys appear to float off the wood or merge into each other. Also, check the bocal insertion point for realistic geometry.
